text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351-7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn, Slovak Premier Vladimir Meciar and Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky will meet in Postyen, Slovakia today to review trilateral cooperation.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn announced Saturday that the government will work out a national agriculture programme to prepare Hungary for membership in the European Union.
- A joint meeting of the Socialist Party presidential board and the Free Democrats executive body to review coalition cooperation is set for Friday.

- Germany has promised to take back a shipment containing 380 tons of industrial chemical agents that has been stranded at the Hungarian-Croat border for months, Germany's environment ministry announced on Sunday.

- "I can see pretty good chances of Hungary becoming a full member of the European Monetary Union within ten years", National Bank President Gyorgy Suranyi said in the weekend edition of the Wall Street Journal Europe.
- A recent study on the former socialist countries put together by EBRD envisages an annual 4-5 per cent GDP growth for Hungary before the turn of the century.

- The Hungarian government is balancing on a narrow plank between sastisfying the IMF's demand for further deficit-reduction measures and strengthening the Socialist Party's popularity for the next elections, according to an analysis by the London office of the investment bank Nomura.

- An unidentified person shot dead Jozsef Prisztas, a close friend of one of a leading figure in the Hungarian underworld on Friday. Police say the battle for territory among some Budapest crime gangs has become an open gang war.
- Hungary's Nandor Fa set sail on Sunday on the Vendee Globe round-the-world yachting race on board his craft Budapest.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The State Securities and Exchange Supervision suspended the trading of Magyar Hitel Bank shares on the OTC market for another further four working days from October 31.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- President Arpad Goncz Friday appointed Dezso Avarkeszi as political state secretary at the Justice Ministry, and Ildiko T. Asztalos as political state secretary at the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism. (Sat.)
- The Young Democrats may uncover another scandal implicating persons close to the coalition when they address Parliament today.

- Inflation will not drop to the level set by the Maastricht Treaty as adequate for joining the EMU before the year 2005, said financial deputy state secretary Tamas Tetenyi at the MoneyMarket '96 conference on Friday. (Sat.)

- Matav CEO Elek Straub took issue with a recent Financial Times report that the Hungarian telephone company's shares will be introduced to the stock exchange within 18 months, saying the details have not yet been worked out, and calling the paper's estimate of the value of the offering "pure speculation".
NAPI GAZDASAG
- More details have become available on Hungary's import and export figures through August, as reported by this paper.
- Truck manufacturer Raba achieved sales of HUF 21.1 billion in the first nine months.
- The German forwarding company Willi Betz Internationale Spedition GmbH has set up a wholly owned subsidiary in Hungary.
